metadata.note: The Syracuse streetcar network -- nine lines, drawn as the system stood in its last decades. Horsecars began Aug 16 1860, when two cars of the Central City Railway came out of their Wolf Street barn onto a mile and a half of iron rail; by 1870 there were twelve miles along North and South Salina and East and West Genesee Streets, and by 1886 over five million riders a year. The first electric trolley ran in 1888 and the last horsecar, on the Green Street line, on Aug 19 1900. The Syracuse Rapid Transit Railway was chartered May 21 1896 out of three predecessor companies, and passed in 1912 to New York State Railways, the New York Central's upstate traction holding company, as its Syracuse Lines. Bus conversion began with the Burnet line in 1933. When the Syracuse Lines were reorganized as the Syracuse Transit Corporation on Nov 22 1939 only seven streetcar routes were left; South Salina and Nedrow went on Jun 29 1940, Elm Street on Nov 11 1940, and Walnut, Westcott, Butternut and Wolf on Jan 4 1941 -- the last day of streetcar operation in Syracuse, marked by cars 1074 and 1078 running coupled as a farewell train. Alignments follow modern street centrelines; the ROUTES THEMSELVES ARE RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE LINE NAMES, not from a route map -- see geometry_quality on each feature and not_yet_sourced below.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Transit_Corporation (the Syracuse Lines of New York State Railways reorganized Nov 22 1939 as the Syracuse Transit Corporation with 27 routes of which seven were streetcar lines; New York State Railways created by the New York Central in 1909, Syracuse Lines under its control from 1912; NYC sold the company 1928, receivership 1929-1934; bus conversion began with the Burnet line in 1933; the University line closed Sep 30 1939; South Salina and Nedrow Jun 29 1940; Elm Street Nov 11 1940; Walnut, Westcott, Butternut and Wolf on Jan 4 1941, the last day, with cars 1074 and 1078 coupled as the final train)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Rapid_Transit_Railway (chartered May 21 1896 as a consolidation of the Syracuse Street Railroad Company, the Syracuse Consolidated Street Railway Company and the People's Railroad Company; consolidated into New York State Railways in 1912)

https://www.cnyhistory.org/2015/03/the-first-modes-of-urban-public-transportation-in-syracuse/ -- Onondaga Historical Association (first horsecars Aug 16 1860, two cars of the Central City Railway from a Wolf Street barn over 1.5 miles of track; twelve miles by 1870 along North and South Salina and East and West Genesee Streets, plus the Oakwood line, the Valley and Solvay; over 5 million riders by 1886; People's Railroad and Consolidated Street Railway consolidations by 1890; first electric trolley 1888; last horsecar on the Green Street line Aug 19 1900)
https://www.openstreetmap.org (ODbL) -- street centrelines used for the routing
metadata.not_yet_sourced: THE ROUTES ARE RECONSTRUCTED, NOT SOURCED. The nine line NAMES and their closure dates are documented; the streets they ran on are inferred from those names, and each line is drawn from the downtown hub at Salina and Genesee out along its namesake street to that street's end. No Sanborn fire insurance sheet, period track map or company timetable has been consulted, so outer termini, downtown approaches, loops, branches and any street the line used that is not its namesake are all unverified. The split between the South Salina and Nedrow lines -- both closed the same day -- is drawn at the city line and is a guess. Individual line OPENING dates are unknown: every feature starts at 1896, the Syracuse Rapid Transit consolidation, although horsecars ran from 1860 and electric cars from 1888, so the early years of these corridors are under-drawn. Every headway is a placeholder, not a timetable, and speeds are estimates. Lines that had already been converted to bus before 1939 are not drawn at all apart from Burnet, because neither their names nor their conversion dates have been established -- the network shown is therefore smaller than the real one.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
